tone_statements.quote: In Kafa, gemination of consonants and lengthening of vowels are phonemic, as is also tone. There are two tones high and low. (Theil 2007: 197-200, Bender 2000:100). sources.citation: Leikola, Kirsi. 2014. Talking Manjo: Linguistic repertoires as means of negotiating marginalization. PhD dissertation, University of Helsinki. 270 pp. (hdl:10138/44772)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Sociolinguistic study; present-day Manjo speak Kafa (Kafi noono) with a recognisable 'accent' (p.124: 'My first impression was that the Manjo have a special accent in their speech..differences in pronunciation and intonation'), implosives per Bender 2000:100, and some special lexicon; Kafa is described as tonal with two tones (p.42, citing Theil 2007, Bender 2000). Mentions the historical Manjo argot/hunter register (Bender 2000:96) but gives no phonological description of it.

tone.quote: In Kafa, gemination of consonants and lengthening of vowels are phonemic, as is also tone. There are two tones high and low. (Theil 2007: 197-200, Bender 2000:100). In the quotations I mention the tone in those cases in which the similarity of the words can cause misunderstanding.
tone.locator: p. 41, end of the paragraph on language learning and transcription in the methods chapter; '197-200' is hyphen-broken across a line
tone.says: P. 41: Kafa, including the Manjo variant transcribed in the thesis, has phonemic tone with two tones, high and low (citing Theil 2007: 197-200 and Bender 2000: 100); tone is unmarked in the school orthography and the author marks it only where homographs could be confused. Applied to Manjo data: p. 69 footnote '*Doollo with high tone, antelope; doollo with low tone, bamboo water container' (in a Manjo elder's speech) and p. 75 fn. 32 'The word is not the same as Manjo; the tone difference makes…
